18|BACKGROUND
19|Establishing cardiovascular safety of new therapies for type 2 diabetes is important.
20|Safety data are available for the subcutaneous form of the glucagon-like peptide-1 recep-
21|tor agonist semaglutide but are needed for oral semaglutide.
22|METHODS
23|We assessed cardiovascular outcomes of once-daily oral semaglutide in an event-driven,
24|randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving patients at high cardiovas-
25|cular risk (age of ≥50 years with established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease, or
26|age of ≥60 years with cardiovascular risk factors only). The primary outcome in a time-
27|to-event analysis was the first occurrence of a major adverse cardiovascular event (death
28|from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke). The
29|trial was designed to rule out 80% excess cardiovascular risk as compared with placebo
30|(noninferiority margin of 1.8 for the upper boundary of the 95% confidence interval for
31|the hazard ratio for the primary outcome).
32|RESULTS
33|A total of 3183 patients were randomly assigned to receive oral semaglutide or placebo. The
34|mean age of the patients was 66 years; 2695 patients (84.7%) were 50 years of age or older
35|and had cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The median time in the trial was 15.9
36|months. Major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 61 of 1591 patients (3.8%) in the
37|oral semaglutide group and 76 of 1592 (4.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95%
38|confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Results for components
39|of the primary outcome were as follows: death from cardiovascular causes, 15 of 1591
40|patients (0.9%) in the oral semaglutide group and 30 of 1592 (1.9%) in the placebo group
41|(hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.27 to 0.92); nonfatal myocardial infarction, 37 of 1591 pa-
42|tients (2.3%) and 31 of 1592 (1.9%), respectively (hazard ratio, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.73 to 1.90);
43|and nonfatal stroke, 12 of 1591 patients (0.8%) and 16 of 1592 (1.0%), respectively (hazard
44|ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.35 to 1.57). Death from any cause occurred in 23 of 1591 patients
45|(1.4%) in the oral semaglutide group and 45 of 1592 (2.8%) in the placebo group (hazard
46|ratio, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.31 to 0.84). Gastrointestinal adverse events leading to discontinu-
47|ation of oral semaglutide or placebo were more common with oral semaglutide.
48|CONCLUSIONS
49|In this trial involving patients with type 2 diabetes, the cardiovascular risk profile of oral
50|semaglutide was not inferior to that of placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; PIONEER 6
51|ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02692716.)

5|ardiovascular disease is the pri-
6|mary cause of death in patients with type 2
7|diabetes,1 and the ruling out of an excess
8|cardiovascular risk is a regulatory requirement
9|for new glucose-lowering therapies.2,3 Glucagon-
10|like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are well-
11|established glucose-lowering medications for the
12|treatment of type 2 diabetes and are associated
13|with reductions in body weight and a low risk of
14|hypoglycemia.4-11 These agents have shown car-
15|diovascular safety (lixisenatide12 and exenatide13)
16|and, in several cases, benefit (liraglutide,14 albi-
17|glutide,15 semaglutide,16 and, most recently, dula
18|glutide17). For example, in the Trial to Evaluate
19|Cardiovascular and Other Long-term Outcomes
20|with Semaglutide in Subjects with Type 2 Diabe-
21|tes (SUSTAIN-6), patients who received a once-
22|weekly subcutaneous injection of semaglutide
23|had a 26% lower risk of the primary cardiovas-
24|cular outcome than those who received placebo.16
25|Recent diabetes and cardiology treatment guide-
26|lines recommend GLP-1 receptor agonists as a
27|second-line treatment option for adults with
28|type 2 diabetes.18,19
29|All currently approved GLP-1 receptor ago-
30|nists are administered subcutaneously. Oral sema-
31|glutide has been developed as a once-daily tab-
32|let, which may allay concerns about injections
33|among some patients and clinicians20 and result
34|in earlier initiation of GLP-1 receptor agonist
35|therapy. As compared with once-weekly subcuta-
36|neous semaglutide, oral semaglutide has a dif-
37|ferent absorption profile.21,22 However, once the
38|drug is absorbed, the pharmacokinetic properties
39|and effects of semaglutide are similar, regard-
40|less of the route of administration.21,22 The present
41|randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3a trial,
42|Peptide Innovation for Early Diabetes Treatment
43|(PIONEER) 6, is a preapproval cardiovascular
44|outcomes trial specifically designed to rule out
45|an excess in cardiovascular risk with oral sema-
46|glutide among patients with type 2 diabetes.
47|Methods
48|Trial Design and Oversight
49|Detailed methods for this trial, which was con-
50|ducted at 214 sites in 21 countries, have been
51|published previously,23 and the protocol is avail-
52|able with the full text of this article at NEJM.org.
53|The sponsor (Novo Nordisk) designed the trial
54|and was responsible for the trial conduct, data
55|collection, and data analysis. An independent
56|data monitoring committee evaluated unblinded
57|trial data.
58|All the authors had full access to the data,
59|participated in drafting or critical revision of
60|the manuscript, made the decision to submit the
61|manuscript for publication, and vouch for the
62|accuracy and completeness of the data and for
63|the adherence of the trial to the protocol. The
64|manuscript was drafted with support from a
65|medical writer (funded by the sponsor), under
66|the direction of the authors.
67|Patients
68|Patients were eligible to participate if they were
69|50 years of age or older and had established
70|cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney dis-
71|ease, or if they were 60 years of age or older and
72|had cardiovascular risk factors only. Key exclu-
73|sion criteria were treatment with any GLP-1 re-
74|ceptor agonist, dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor,
75|or pramlintide within 90 days before screening;
76|New York Heart Association class 4 heart failure;
77|planned coronary-artery, carotid-artery, or periph-
78|eral-artery revascularization; myocardial infarc-
79|tion, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable an-
80|gina or transient ischemic attack within 60 days
81|before screening; long-term or intermittent hemo-
82|dialysis or peritoneal dialysis, or severe renal
83|impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate
84|[GFR], <30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-
85|surface area); and proliferative retinopathy or
86|maculopathy resulting in active treatment. The
87|full eligibility criteria are provided in the Supple-
88|mentary Appendix, available at NEJM.org.
89|Procedures
90|Patients were randomly assigned (in a 1:1 ratio)
91|to receive once-daily oral semaglutide (target
92|dose, 14 mg) or placebo (Fig. S1 in the Supple-
93|mentary Appendix), both in addition to standard-
94|of-care treatment, in a double-blind fashion.
95|Randomization was stratified according to evi-
96|dence of established cardiovascular disease or
97|chronic kidney disease or the presence of cardio-
98|vascular risk factors only.
99|Patients were instructed to take oral semaglu-
100|tide or placebo in the morning, with up to 120 ml
101|of water, in a fasting state, and at least 30 min-
102|utes before eating, drinking, or taking any other
103|oral medication. A dose-escalation schedule was
104|used to decrease gastrointestinal side effects.23
105|Once the desired dose was reached, patients re-
106|mained at the maximum 14-mg daily dose unless

17|Outcomes
18|The primary outcome was the time from random-
19|ization to the first occurrence of a major adverse
20|cardiovascular event, a composite of death from
21|cardiovascular causes (including undetermined
22|causes of death), nonfatal myocardial infarction,
23|or nonfatal stroke. Secondary cardiovascular out-
24|comes included the time from randomization to
25|the first occurrence of the following: an expanded
26|composite outcome consisting of the primary
27|outcome plus unstable angina resulting in hos-
28|pitalization or heart failure resulting in hospital-
29|ization; a composite of death from any cause,
30|nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke;
31|and the individual components of these compos-
32|ite outcomes. Additional efficacy outcomes in-
33|cluded the change from baseline to the end of
34|the treatment period in the glycated hemoglobin
35|level, body weight, and lipid levels.
36|A select set of safety outcomes was investi-
37|gated, encompassing adverse events leading to
38|discontinuation of semaglutide or placebo, serious
39|adverse events, and adverse events of special in-
40|terest (including diabetic retinopathy assessed by
41|scheduled eye examinations, and severe hypogly-
42|cemic episodes). Cardiovascular and other selected
43|events were adjudicated by an independent, exter-
44|nal event-adjudication committee whose members
45|were unaware of the trial-group assignments.
46|Statistical Analysis
47|The statistical methods have been reported pre-
48|viously,23 and further information is provided in
49|the Supplementary Appendix and below. Our
50|trial was an event-driven trial designed to rule
51|out an 80% excess in cardiovascular risk with
52|oral semaglutide by assessment of noninferiority
53|to placebo for the primary outcome (noninferior-
54|ity margin of 1.8 for the upper boundary of the
55|95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio).
56|The trial continued until accrual of at least 122
57|events, with no predefined minimum duration.
58|All analyses involved the full analysis set,
59|which included all randomly assigned patients.
60|The primary outcome encompassed events oc-
61|curring between randomization and the final
62|follow-up visit (aligned at 5 weeks after the last
63|trial-wide assigned dose, except for patients who
64|withdrew from the trial).
65|A stratified Cox proportional-hazards model
66|was used for the primary outcome analysis, with
67|trial group as a fixed factor. Conditional to con-
68|firmation of noninferiority, superiority testing
69|was performed on the primary outcome. Analyses
70|of all other outcomes were not controlled for
71|multiple comparisons and should be interpreted
72|as exploratory. Prespecified sensitivity and sub-
73|group analyses explored the robustness of the
74|primary outcome analysis. Secondary efficacy
75|outcomes and adverse events were assessed by
76|means of descriptive statistics.
77|Results
78|Patients
79|Between January and August 2017, a total of
80|3183 patients were randomly assigned to oral
81|semaglutide (1591 patients) or placebo (1592 pa-
82|tients). The median time in the trial (including
83|follow-up) was 15.9 months (range, 0.4 to 20.0),
84|and approximately 75% of the patients received
85|oral semaglutide or placebo for more than 1 year.
86|In total, 3172 patients (99.7%) completed the
87|trial; 1347 (84.7%) completed the trial regimen
88|with oral semaglutide and 1435 (90.1%) with
89|placebo (Fig. S2 in the Supplementary Appen-
90|dix). Vital-status information was collected for
91|the 11 patients who did not complete the trial,
92|thus accounting for all patients who took part.

94|oral semaglutide who completed the trial regi-

96|at the end of the treatment period (Fig. S3 in the
97|Supplementary Appendix).

48|Efficacy Outcomes
49|Glycated hemoglobin levels decreased more in
50|the oral semaglutide group than in the placebo
51|group (mean change from baseline to end of
52|trial, -1.0 vs. -0.3 percentage points), as did
53|body weight (mean change from baseline to end
54|of trial, -4.2 kg vs. -0.8 kg) (Fig. 2, and Fig. S7
55|in the Supplementary Appendix). Systolic blood
56|pressure decreased more in the oral semaglutide
57|group than in the placebo group (Table S4 in
58|the Supplementary Appendix), and levels of
59|low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglyc-
60|erides were modestly lower in the oral sema-
61|glutide group (Fig. S8 in the Supplementary
62|Appendix).
63|Adverse Events and Safety
64|Serious adverse events occurred in 301 of 1591
65|patients (18.9%) in the oral semaglutide group
66|and 358 of 1592 (22.5%) in the placebo group
67|(Table 3). Serious adverse events were varied and
68|involved several organ systems (Table S5 in the
69|Supplementary Appendix).
70|More patients permanently discontinued oral
71|semaglutide than placebo (184 of 1591 patients
72|[11.6%] vs. 104 of 1592 [6.5%]) (Table 3, and
73|Table S6 in the Supplementary Appendix). This
74|difference was driven by gastrointestinal adverse
75|events (in 108 of 1591 patients [6.8%] in the oral
76|semaglutide group vs. in 26 of 1592 [1.6%] in
77|the placebo group) (Table 3), primarily nausea
78|(in 46 of 1591 patients [2.9%] vs. in 8 of 1592
79|[0.5%]), vomiting (in 24 of 1591 patients [1.5%]
80|vs. in 4 of 1592 [0.3%]), and diarrhea (in 22 of
81|1591 patients [1.4%] vs. in 6 of 1592 [0.4%]),
82|mostly nonserious. However, serious adverse
83|events led to permanent discontinuation of oral
84|semaglutide in 41 of 1591 patients (2.6%) and of
85|placebo in 48 of 1592 patients (3.0%).
86|There were 68 deaths during the trial (in 23
87|of 1591 patients in the oral semaglutide group
88|and in 45 of 1592 in the placebo group). The
89|most frequent underlying causes of death were
90|cardiovascular (in 10 of 23 deaths with oral
91|semaglutide and in 23 of 45 deaths with place-
92|bo) (Table S7 in the Supplementary Appendix).
93|There was no clustering of causes among deaths
94|from noncardiovascular causes.

3|STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
4|The trial was designed to exclude an 80% excess in cardiovascular risk for oral semaglutide
5|compared with placebo (defined as the upper limit of the two-sided 95% confidence interval
6|not exceeding 1.8) in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk. Analysis of
7|the primary outcome (time from randomization to first major cardiovascular event)
8|encompassed events occurring between randomization and the final follow-up visit. Because
9|the time of randomization varied between patients, the final follow-up visits were aligned at 5
10|weeks after the last trial-wide trial product dose (with the exception of patients who withdrew
11|from the trial). A stratified Cox proportional hazards model was used for the primary analysis,
12|with treatment group as a fixed factor, and stratification based on evidence of cardiovascular
13|disease/advanced chronic kidney disease at screening. Patients who did not have a primary
14|outcome event during the in-trial period were censored at the final follow-up visit, or at time
15|of withdrawal for patients who withdrew from the trial.
16|Testing was hierarchical: following confirmation of non-inferiority, a test for superiority versus
17|placebo was performed, thereby preserving the type 1 error in the strong sense at 5% (two-
18|sided). All primary and secondary analyses were performed on the full analysis set, including
19|all randomized patients.
20|Sensitivity analyses tested the robustness of the primary analysis. One sensitivity analysis
21|included additional covariates (sex, region, baseline age, diabetes duration, smoking history,
22|and baseline renal function). The other two sensitivity analyses were based on the treatment
23|effect prior to any permanent discontinuation of trial product and focused on events
24|occurring during the on-treatment observation period (from first date of trial product
25|administration to the date of last dose plus 38 days or final follow-up visit [whichever was
26|first]), and the on-treatment observation period using a narrower period (+7 days) after the
27|last of trial product, respectively. Patients without an event were censored at the end of the
28|observation period. All sensitivity analyses were performed using the full analysis set and the
29|same model as the analysis of the primary outcome, including censoring rules and
